subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Sharenting
description: A quick, practical guide to Sharenting.

hook.text: By age five, the average child has 1,500 photos of themselves posted online — by their own parents.

buildup.text: Sharenting — parents sharing children's photos and stories online — creates a digital footprint before consent.

discovery.text: These photos feed facial recognition databases and are scraped by data companies and AI trainers.

twist.text: Children grow up to find their childhood documented publicly. Some sue their parents over it.

climax.text: Parents create digital identities for children who never consented. The footprint can't be erased.

punchline.text: Born digital. No say in the matter.

quiz.question: What is 'sharenting'?
options: Parents sharing their children's photos and stories online
Children sharing their own content on social media
